markdown_content: # Skill Up: CLO LiveSync for Unreal Engine This document provides a detailed guide on using the CLO LiveSync plugin with Unreal Engine 5 (UE5), covering installation, setup, optimization, import/export processes, material adjustments, environment creation with Quixel Bridge, and MetaHuman avatar integration. Key terms include Unreal Engine 5, CLO LiveSync plugin, Substance plugin, geometry cache, material instances, Quixel Bridge, and MetaHuman. --- ## Introduction to Unreal Engine 5 and Its Relevance to Fashion Industry This section explains Unreal Engine 5’s origins, features, and its application in the fashion industry, emphasizing real-time photorealistic rendering with Lumen and the benefits of integrating CLO garments into UE5. - **Unreal Engine History and Development**: Created by Epic Games in 1998 as a graphics engine for video games, it has evolved into a real-time 3D visualization platform widely used across industries including automotive, virtual production, product visualization, AR/VR, and mobile apps. - **Unreal Engine 5 Improvements**: Released in April 2022, UE5 offers significant enhancements for photorealistic real-time rendering, primarily through the Lumen system which provides global illumination and ray tracing. - **Fashion Industry Benefits**: Unlike conventional render engines that require lengthy processing, UE5 allows real-time rendering of complex garments and animations, enabling faster iteration of multiple colorways and details. - **Content Library**: Epic Games provides Quixel Bridge, a vast library of 3D assets and materials, plus MetaHuman avatar integration for ultra-realistic digital humans. --- ## CLO LiveSync Plugin: Purpose and Installation This section covers the purpose of the CLO LiveSync plugin, its installation steps, and prerequisite plugins. - **Purpose**: The plugin bridges CLO 7.3 and Unreal Engine 5 (version 5.3 or newer), enabling seamless transfer of garments, avatars, and animations without manual exports (OBJ, FBX, Alembic) or material adjustments. - **Installation**: 1. Download the latest CLO LiveSync plugin from the CLO website under "Connect". 2. Extract the downloaded folder. 3. Copy the extracted plugin folder into `Program Files\Epic Games\Unreal Engine\[version]\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace`. 4. Install the Substance 3D plugin via the Epic Games Launcher Marketplace to enable proper shader functionality. - **Activation**: - Open Unreal Engine. - In the project, go to **Settings > Plugins**. - Ensure both CLO LiveSync and Substance plugins are installed and activated. - Restart Unreal Engine after enabling plugins. --- ## Unreal Engine Project Setup for CLO LiveSync This section outlines necessary Unreal Engine project settings for stability and proper garment transparency display. - **Project Settings**: - Set **Render Hardware Interface (RHI)** to **DirectX 11** (downgrade from default DirectX 12) to avoid potential crashes or freezes. - Enable **Order-Independent Transparency** for translucent surfaces to correctly render fabric transparency. - **Restart** Unreal Engine after applying these changes. - **Starting a Project**: Recommended starting template is "Automotive Product Design (Blank)" due to its clean setup with a camera and basic lighting. --- ## CLO Project Optimization Before LiveSync This section describes best practices in CLO to reduce polygon count and optimize garment performance for Unreal Engine. - **Topstitch Optimization**: - Convert 3D topstitch objects from "OBJ" type (which adds many polygons) to "Texture" type to reduce polygon count. - **Mesh Optimization**: - Select all pattern pieces. - In the property editor under *Miscellaneous*, change the mesh type from **Triangles** to **Quads** to reduce vertex and face count while preserving detail. - **Saving**: Save the CLO project after optimization before syncing with Unreal Engine. --- ## Using CLO LiveSync: Importing Garments and Avatars into Unreal Engine This section explains the LiveSync workflow, garment and avatar import options, and interaction with the 3D viewport in Unreal Engine. - **Starting LiveSync**: - Click the **Live Sync** button in CLO. - Confirm simulation is turned off (no animation recording or UV editor mode active). - Wait for the update progress to reach 100%; initial transfer may take time depending on particle distance, texture resolution, and PC speed. - **Unreal Engine Viewport Navigation**: - Left-click garment and press **F** to focus. - Hold **Alt + Left Mouse Button** to rotate. - Hold **Alt + Right Mouse Button** to zoom. - Hold **Alt + Middle Mouse Button** to pan. - Alternatively, use **W, A, S, D, Q, E** while holding the right mouse button for game-style navigation. - **Import Options**: - **Garment**: - Save as **Static Mesh** (geometry only). - Save as **Geometry Cache** (includes animation). - **Avatar**: - Save as **Static Mesh**. - Save as **Skeletal Mesh** (includes rig for animation). - **Export Process**: - Geometry cache export runs in the background, no manual Alembic export needed. - After export, import the file from the project’s content folder into Unreal Engine by dragging it into the scene. --- ## Material Instances and Shader Adjustments in Unreal Engine This section details handling garment materials, adjusting textures, and manipulating material properties via material instances. - **Material Instances**: - Each geometry cache includes material instances for each fabric. - Material instances simplify complex shader node trees into adjustable parameters such as normal map intensity and base color. - **Adjusting Normal Map Intensity**: - Open the material instance for a fabric. - Scroll to the normal map intensity slider and increase it to enhance fabric texture realism. - **Changing Fabric Colors**: - Modify the base color property within the material instance color field. - Apply new tint colors easily without complex shader edits. --- ## Creating and Managing Environment Assets Using Quixel Bridge This section explains how to use Quixel Bridge inside Unreal Engine to add realistic 3D environment assets, including rocks and plants, to your scene. - **Accessing Quixel Bridge**: - Open the content drawer. - Click **Add > Quixel Bridge Content**. - Log in with Epic Games credentials if prompted. - **Searching and Downloading Assets**: - Search keywords like "rock" to find 3D models or surface materials. - Download and add assets to your project. - **Importing Assets**: - Locate downloaded assets in the Megascans folder in the content drawer. - Select static mesh and drag it into the scene. - **Duplicating and Transforming Assets**: - Hold **Alt** and use arrow keys on the gizmo to duplicate. - Use **Space** to toggle between move, rotate, and scale gizmos. - Right-click assets for transform options such as mirroring. - **Foliage Tool for Plants**: - Switch to **Foliage Mode** from the top bar. - Select foliage assets (trees, plants) from Megascans 3D plants folder. - Adjust brush size and scale variation. - Paint foliage onto surfaces by brushing. - Reset location coordinates to (0, 0, 0). - **Sequencer Setup and Animation**: - Create a new level sequence (recommended organized folder structure). - Drag MetaHuman from outliner into Sequencer timeline. - Use Unreal’s default mannequin animations as source. - Retarget animation to MetaHuman rig. - Apply animations such as idle or walking. - Export retargeted animations as Animation Sequence. - Use LiveSync to update MetaHuman with new animations in CLO. --- ## Workflow Summary and Best Practices This final section summarizes the core workflow and important considerations for efficient use of CLO LiveSync and Unreal Engine. - chunks.content: # Skill Up: CLO LiveSync for Unreal Engine This document provides a detailed guide on using the CLO LiveSync plugin with Unreal Engine 5 (UE5), covering installation, setup, optimization, import/export processes, material adjustments, environment creation with Quixel Bridge, and MetaHuman avatar integration. Key terms include Unreal Engine 5, CLO LiveSync plugin, Substance plugin, geometry cache, material instances, Quixel Bridge, and MetaHuman. --- ## Introduction to Unreal Engine 5 and Its Relevance to Fashion Industry This section explains Unreal Engine 5’s origins, features, and its application in the fashion industry, emphasizing real-time photorealistic rendering with Lumen and the benefits of integrating CLO garments into UE5. - **Unreal Engine History and Development**: Created by Epic Games in 1998 as a graphics engine for video games, it has evolved into a real-time 3D visualization platform widely used across industries including automotive, virtual production, product visualization, AR/VR, and mobile apps. - **Unreal Engine 5 Improvements**: Released in April 2022, UE5 offers significant enhancements for photorealistic real-time rendering, primarily through the Lumen system which provides global illumination and ray tracing. - **Fashion Industry Benefits**: Unlike conventional render engines that require lengthy processing, UE5 allows real-time rendering of complex garments and animations, enabling faster iteration of multiple colorways and details. - **Content Library**: Epic Games provides Quixel Bridge, a vast library of 3D assets and materials, plus MetaHuman avatar integration for ultra-realistic digital humans. --- ## CLO LiveSync Plugin: Purpose and Installation This section covers the purpose of the CLO LiveSync plugin, its installation steps, and prerequisite plugins. - **Purpose**: The plugin bridges CLO 7.3 and Unreal Engine 5 (version 5.3 or newer), enabling seamless transfer of garments, avatars, and animations without manual exports (OBJ, FBX, Alembic) or material adjustments. - **Installation**: 1. Download the latest CLO LiveSync plugin from the CLO website under "Connect". 2. Extract the downloaded folder. 3. Copy the extracted plugin folder into `Program Files\Epic Games\Unreal Engine\[version]\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace`. 4. Install the Substance 3D plugin via the Epic Games Launcher Marketplace to enable proper shader functionality. - **Activation**: - Open Unreal Engine. - In the project, go to **Settings > Plugins**. - Ensure both CLO LiveSync and Substance plugins are installed and activated. - Restart Unreal Engine after enabling plugins. --- ## Unreal Engine Project Setup for CLO LiveSync This section outlines necessary Unreal Engine project settings for stability and proper garment transparency display. - **Project Settings**: - Set **Render Hardware Interface (RHI)** to **DirectX 11** (downgrade from default DirectX 12) to avoid potential crashes or freezes. - Enable **Order-Independent Transparency** for translucent surfaces to correctly render fabric transparency. - **Restart** Unreal Engine after applying these changes. - **Starting a Project**: Recommended starting template is "Automotive Product Design (Blank)" due to its clean setup with a camera and basic lighting. --- ## CLO Project Optimization Before LiveSync This section describes best practices in CLO to reduce polygon count and optimize garment performance for Unreal Engine.

initial transfer may take time depending on particle distance, texture resolution, and PC speed. - **Unreal Engine Viewport Navigation**: - Left-click garment and press **F** to focus. - Hold **Alt + Left Mouse Button** to rotate. - Hold **Alt + Right Mouse Button** to zoom. - Hold **Alt + Middle Mouse Button** to pan. - Alternatively, use **W, A, S, D, Q, E** while holding the right mouse button for game-style navigation. - **Import Options**: - **Garment**: - Save as **Static Mesh** (geometry only). - Save as **Geometry Cache** (includes animation). - **Avatar**: - Save as **Static Mesh**. - Save as **Skeletal Mesh** (includes rig for animation). - **Export Process**: - Geometry cache export runs in the background, no manual Alembic export needed. - After export, import the file from the project’s content folder into Unreal Engine by dragging it into the scene. --- ## Material Instances and Shader Adjustments in Unreal Engine This section details handling garment materials, adjusting textures, and manipulating material properties via material instances. - **Material Instances**: - Each geometry cache includes material instances for each fabric. - Material instances simplify complex shader node trees into adjustable parameters such as normal map intensity and base color. - **Adjusting Normal Map Intensity**: - Open the material instance for a fabric. - Scroll to the normal map intensity slider and increase it to enhance fabric texture realism. - **Changing Fabric Colors**: - Modify the base color property within the material instance color field. - Apply new tint colors easily without complex shader edits.
